x-m-m1-01.title: Finding number with 12 divisors
x-m-m1-01.goal: Find how divisors build from prime-factorized form, then find different numbers meeting condition and check dem.
x-m-m1-01.material:
Number N don get prime factorized, and its only prime factors na 2 and 3. So N be product of '2 multiplied a times' and '3 multiplied b times' (a and b natural numbers at least 1).
For example, 12 = 2²×3 (2 multiply twice, 3 multiply once). If we write divisors of 12 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12) as 'how many times 2 multiplied and how many times 3 multiplied,' we get this:
Divisor 1: 2 zero times, 3 zero times / Divisor 2: 1 time, 0 times / Divisor 4: 2 times, 0 times / Divisor 3: 0 times, 1 time / Divisor 6: 1 time, 1 time / Divisor 12: 2 times, 1 time

x-m-m1-01.s.s1.o.c: Number of ways to pair one of counts 0, 1, 2 for 2 with one of counts 0, 1 for 3
x-m-m1-01.s.s1.r.c: You read each divisor in table as 'pair of two counts' and find the pattern.

x-m-m1-01.s.s2.prompt: Find 3 different numbers N wey get exactly 12 divisors. Enter the two counts wey make N: a (how many times 2 multiply) and b (how many times 3 multiply).

x-m-m1-01.s.s2.ok.c1: a and b na natural numbers at least 1.
x-m-m1-01.s.s2.fail.c1: a and b must be natural numbers at least 1.
x-m-m1-01.s.s2.explain: Examples: (a=3, b=2) give N=72, with 4×3=12 divisors; (5, 1) give N=96; (2, 3) give N=108; (1, 5) give N=486. (3, 2) and (2, 3) give different numbers.

x-m-m1-01.s.s2.because.model.0: 72=2³×3², so count of 2s get 4 choices (0, 1, 2, 3) and count of 3s get 3 choices (0, 1, 2). Pair them and multiply: 4×3=12 divisors.
x-m-m1-01.s.s2.because.model.1: I list divisors of 72 myself: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72. Total na 12.

x-m-m1-05.title: Choosing expression for matchstick pattern
x-m-m1-05.goal: Compare different pattern expressions, choose with reason which always correct, explain risk of expression working for only few values.
x-m-m1-05.material: Squares join in one horizontal row using matchsticks. Neighbor squares share one side. One square need 4 matchsticks, 2 squares take 7, and 3 squares take 10. Matchsticks for n squares shown with 5 formulas a-e.

x-m-m1-05.s.s1.hint.1: For formulas correct at n=1, check n=2 and n=3 too. No decide from only one value.
x-m-m1-05.s.s1.r.a: Check whether you miss brackets when putting 4 for each square and subtracting the (n−1) overlaps. Check whether the value is 4 when n=1.
x-m-m1-05.s.s1.r.b: You put n=1, 2, 3 and got 4, 7, 10, so your reason strong.
x-m-m1-05.s.s1.r.c: You read am with rule say first square need 4 and each extra square add 3.
